title: China Expands Travel Restrictions to AI Talent at Private Tech Firms — DeepSeek, Alibaba Employees Require Government Approval to Travel Abroad
detail: China's government has expanded overseas travel restrictions to cover senior AI researchers and engineers at private-sector technology companies including Alibaba and DeepSeek, Bloomberg reported on May 26, 2026. Employees working on advanced AI models and deemed strategically important must now obtain government approval before traveling abroad — an extension of restrictions previously applied mainly to state employees, nuclear scientists, defense researchers, and academics in sensitive programs. The move represents a formal reclassification of commercial AI talent as a strategically controlled national resource, consistent with Beijing's growing treatment of AI capabilities as a matter of national security requiring state-level protection. The specific scope of the restrictions — which seniority levels are covered, which technical roles qualify, how approval is granted — has not been officially confirmed or publicly released by the Chinese government, and the initial Bloomberg report noted that affected companies have not publicly commented. The expansion arrives as DeepSeek closes its first external funding round led by China's national Big Fund ($10B, ~$50B valuation) — formalizing DeepSeek as a state-strategic AI asset whose talent pool Beijing now explicitly controls. It also comes one week after the May 14–15 Trump-Xi summit established a formal US-China AI safety dialogue, signaling that even as diplomatic AI channels open, Beijing is simultaneously hardening its domestic controls on the people and institutions that produce its AI advantage. The travel restriction expansion is a structural complement to the funding round: the Big Fund inflows retain DeepSeek's researchers financially, while the travel restrictions ensure those researchers cannot be recruited away by international competitors.

media.caption: Bloomberg: China expands overseas travel restrictions to senior AI engineers at private firms including DeepSeek and Alibaba — formal designation of commercial AI talent as a controlled national resource

title: DeepSeek Makes 75% Price Cut on V4 Pro Permanent — $0.003625/M Input Tokens, Deepening Global AI Price War Against OpenAI and US Rivals
detail: DeepSeek permanently slashed the price of its flagship V4 Pro model by 75%, converting what had been a promotional discount set to expire May 31, 2026 into its permanent pricing tier, Bloomberg and multiple outlets confirmed on May 26. New standard pricing ranges from $0.003625 per million input tokens (cache hits) to $0.87 per million output tokens — making DeepSeek V4 Pro less than one-tenth the cost of OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and meaningfully below Chinese rival Kimi at scale. The price cut deepens a global AI price war that DeepSeek initiated in January 2025 with the R1 model's release, and intensifies pressure on every enterprise AI provider competing for API market share. The timing — as DeepSeek is finalizing its first external funding round at ~$50B valuation — signals that the company has calculated competitive pricing as its primary market penetration strategy rather than near-term margin: consistent with founder Liang Wenfeng's May 22 declaration that the company will prioritize groundbreaking research over commercialization. Caixin Global reported the price cut is directly connected to the funding round's closing timeline, as DeepSeek seeks to maximize API adoption before competition from DeepSeek V5 (anticipated H2 2026) complicates the market position of V4 Pro. The 75% permanent reduction also applies downward pressure on Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu's ERNIE API pricing — both companies have been forced to slash prices repeatedly since January 2025 as DeepSeek's efficiency advantage drives China's domestic AI API prices toward commodity levels. Semafor noted that V4 Pro's pricing is now below the compute cost that Western AI companies estimate for running similar-capability models, reinforcing DeepSeek's training efficiency as a structural rather than a temporary competitive moat.

media.caption: Bloomberg: DeepSeek makes permanent 75% discount on flagship V4 Pro AI model — $0.003625/M tokens, less than one-tenth of OpenAI GPT-5.5 pricing, as global AI price war deepens
Semafor: DeepSeek V4 Pro permanently priced below Western rivals' compute cost — structural efficiency moat driving commodity AI API pricing globally

title: Qualcomm Strikes ASIC Chip Supply Deal with ByteDance — First Major External AI Data Center Chip Partnership for TikTok Parent
detail: Qualcomm reached an agreement with TikTok parent ByteDance to supply custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for AI data center infrastructure, Bloomberg reported on May 26, 2026. ByteDance designed the chips in-house; Qualcomm's role in the partnership is to manufacture them at scale — a fabless-plus-foundry arrangement that marks ByteDance's first major external chip supplier relationship for AI infrastructure. The deal falls within permitted US export control thresholds and does not involve restricted chip architectures. Qualcomm shares jumped approximately 6.8% to an all-time high on the announcement, signaling market confidence in Qualcomm's strategic expansion from smartphone applications processors into AI data center silicon — a market that Qualcomm has historically trailed Nvidia and custom ASIC houses like Broadcom and Marvell. The ByteDance-Qualcomm deal is architecturally distinct from ByteDance's $5.6 billion Huawei Ascend 950PR procurement (April 29, 2026), which addresses ByteDance's frontier AI training and large-model inference needs. The Qualcomm ASIC partnership covers a different workload tier — likely inference optimization and serving at lower power-per-token cost — consistent with ByteDance's strategy of maintaining a multi-vendor AI chip stack rather than single-vendor dependence. The deal is also strategically notable as a US company securing a major AI hardware contract with the world's highest-token-volume AI platform despite China's push for domestic chip sourcing: ByteDance's $29.4B 2026 AI capex is predominantly directed at Huawei Ascend domestically, but the Qualcomm partnership demonstrates that Chinese tech giants retain room for US-sourced specialized silicon below the export control threshold. Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon has targeted AI data center as a $6B+ TAM for Qualcomm by 2028; the ByteDance deal validates that strategy with one of the world's largest AI compute consumers.

media.caption: Bloomberg: Qualcomm strikes AI data center ASIC chip supply deal with ByteDance — Qualcomm shares jump 6.8% to all-time high on first major AI infrastructure partnership
